transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-22
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Ravi Shah (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Sapphire Lead Engineer), Tom Wu (Sapphire DevOps), Priya Nair (Sapphire Product)

Summary:
Quick SDK walkthrough for Redwood API + Console + Optimize. Focus was on Python and TypeScript quickstarts, auth options (API key vs SSO), env setup, and next steps for a pilot and performance benchmarks. Some audio glitches; auto-transcript had a few name mis-transcribes.

Topics:
- SDK quickstarts (python/typescript)
- Authentication patterns and env vars
- Console walkthrough: keys, routes, usage
- Redwood Optimize suggestions and profiling
- Pilot scope and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Ava from Redwood, I'm the AE, with Ravi our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Lena: Hey Ava, thanks, we're good. Excited to see the SDK. Quick note we have Tom and Priya on the line as well.
[00:10] Ravi: Great, we'll jump into a live walkthrough. We'll cover the Python and TypeScript SDKs, auth, environment variables, and then show how Console ties into the quickstart and Optimize recommendations.
[00:20] Tom: Quick ask before we start - we run in a VPC and we care about private deployment options. Hoping to understand auth and network setup too.
[00:27] Ava: Totally, we'll touch on Private deployment considerations and the Console admin flow for Dedicated and Private. Ravi, take it away.
[00:35] Ravi: Cool. So first up, Python quickstart. The SDK is pip-installable, um often shows up in the docs. The base pattern is set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your env and then instantiate a client. Example: client = Redwood(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY']).
[00:55] Lena: Sorry can you show the code again? The transcript sometimes garbles underscores.
[00:58] Ravi: Yeah, sure. I'll paste the gist in the chat after. For TS it's basically the same: import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
[01:15] Priya: Do you recommend service-account style keys scoped per-team or a single org key for initial testing?
[01:20] Ava: For pilots we usually recommend a scoped API key per project so you can track usage per team. For long-term orgs often use integration with SSO and short-lived tokens.
[01:30] Tom: And for Private deployments, how does auth look? We need SSO and KMS integration.
[01:35] Ravi: Private gives you a control plane in your VPC, and we integrate with customer SSO for console access (SAML/Okta) and KMS for key material. For runtime auth you can still use API keys issued by your private control plane or short-lived tokens via an OIDC flow.
[01:50] Lena: That sounds good. Can you show the Console where keys are created?
[01:55] Ravi: Yep - switching to the Console. (screen share gap, 10s) Here under Org Settings -> API Keys, you can create scoped keys, set expiration, and attach tags for team attribution. There's also a key rotation UI.
[02:20] Priya: Any RBAC? We want devs to call APIs but only admins to create keys.
[02:24] Ava: Yes, Console supports RBAC, role-based permissions; we'll share the doc link. (link: https://docs.redwood.com/console/rbac)
[02:35] Tom: Ok, network - do we need a NAT or can we route via private endpoints?
[02:40] Ravi: For Private, we recommend private endpoints inside the VPC; you can also use NAT if needed for certain integrations. We'll send the VPC networking diagram after the call.
[02:50] Lena: Back to SDK, how do we handle streaming responses in the SDKs?
[02:55] Ravi: In Python we expose a stream iterator so you can do for chunk in client.generate_stream(...): process(chunk). In TS the SDK exposes an async iterator or a WebSocket/Server-Sent Events option for lower-latency streaming.
[03:15] Priya: Do you have built-in retry and backoff in the SDK?
[03:18] Ravi: Yes there's a small builtin retry with exponential backoff configurable per-client. For high-throughput we recommend the batch endpoints and also the Redwood Optimize suggestions.
[03:30] Ava: Quick pause - I know you mentioned cost tradeoffs. We should capture your traffic profile so we can suggest batching and quantization recommendations.
[03:38] Lena: We'll put that in the repo we promised to share.
[03:42] Ravi: Great. Now I'll demo a tiny TS quickstart - creating a client, calling generation, and capturing tokens. (reads code aloud) import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: 'us-west-2' });
[04:05] Ravi: Then await client.generate({ model: 'rw-7b', prompt: 'Summarize this...', max_tokens: 150 });
[04:12] Tom: Do you expose token-level cost estimation?
[04:15] Ravi: In Console we have token breakdowns and per-route cost. SDK returns usage metadata so you can log tokens per request.
[04:25] Priya: Any examples of embedding flows? We're planning semantic search for docs.
[04:30] Ravi: Yes, there's an embeddings client: client.embeddings.create({ model:'rw-embed-1', input: ['doc1','doc2'] }). It returns vectors and usage. We'll include the embeddings quickstart.
[04:45] Ava: I'll note that Optimize can recommend batching windows for embeddings to reduce unit costs.
[04:50] Lena: On deployments, do you do A/B rollouts between model versions?
[04:55] Ravi: Yes, Console supports rollouts/canary: route x% to new model, automatic fallback. We'll demo that in a follow-up deeper session.
[05:05] Priya: Are there SDK samples for error handling when a model fails over to a smaller variant?
[05:10] Ravi: We have patterns: check response.status or client.throw_on_error flag; fallback hooks in the SDK let you intercept and retry against a configured fallback model.
[05:20] Tom: About secrets - are keys stored locally or do you recommend using KMS/secret manager integrations?
[05:25] Ava: For production, definitely use your cloud secret manager and reference via env or use workload identity. For Private we support KMS/HSM integration as Ravi mentioned.
[05:35] (static) [05:40] Lena: Are there rate limits we'd hit on hosted if we scale to 2k rps?
[05:45] Ravi: Hosted has tiers; for 2k rps we'd recommend Dedicated reserved pools. We can size GPU pools based on tokens/sec. We'll include a capacity estimate spreadsheet.
[06:00] Priya: Great. Can you discuss security docs - SOC 2, ISO, audit logs?
[06:05] Ava: Yep, we have SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and per-request audit logs in Private and Dedicated. I'll attach the security pack after the call. (link: https://redwood.com/security-pack)
[06:18] Lena: Perfect. A few micro-questions from our engineers: 1) Does the SDK run in serverless functions? 2) Any node runtime requirements for TS?
[06:28] Ravi: 1) Yes, we see customers call from lambda/Cloud Functions, just be mindful of cold-starts and token caching. 2) For TS/Node we support Node 16+. We recommend keeping persistent connections for streaming use.
[06:38] Tom: Do you offer on-prem builds we can air-gap?
[06:41] Ava: Yes, we have an on-prem package; packaging and licensing is part of the Private offering. We'll discuss contract terms if you want to go that route.
[06:50] (10 min jump for brevity in transcript) [16:50] Ravi: Picking back up - showing the Console Quickstarts page now. It includes copy/paste snippets for Python and TS, env var setup instructions, and a sample docker-compose for local dev.
[17:05] Ravi: The Python snippet uses requests under the hood for sync calls and an aiohttp-based client for async streaming.
[17:15] Priya: Can we see an example of env var names? We standardize envs in our deploys.
[17:18] Ravi: Sure - REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_REGION, REDWOOD_MODEL_OVERRIDE are common. Also REDWOOD_ORG_ID for multi-tenant setups.
[17:30] Lena: For logging and observability can we forward traces to our existing APM?
[17:34] Ravi: Yes, we emit traces and provide tracing hooks. The Console supports OTLP ingestion and also exports to common platforms. We'll share the tracing guide link.
[17:45] Priya: The Optimize feature you mentioned - is that an auto config or suggestion engine?
[17:50] Ravi: It's a recommendations engine that looks at your traffic patterns - sequence length distribution, latency SLOs, and suggests batching window sizes, cache prefixes to enable, and quantization profiles for models. It produces a set of actionable changes you can apply in Console.
[18:10] Tom: If we apply an Optimize suggestion and it affects quality, is there a rollback?
[18:13] Ravi: Yes, changes are versioned and you can rollback and have canary testing before global rollout.
[18:20] Lena: Any gotchas when moving from a dev org to Dedicated? We want minimal code changes.
[18:25] Ava: The client config is the same; mostly the endpoint and API key source changes. We'll provide migration steps in the quickstart.
[18:35] (small crosstalk) [18:40] Priya: Regarding embeddings - do you recommend storing vectors as float32 or quantized? We care about storage costs.
[18:45] Ravi: Depends on retrieval accuracy - Optimize can recommend Q4_0 or Q4_K profiles if you want 8-bit storage savings; it will run sample evals to estimate quality loss.
[18:58] Lena: Ok, timeline - we want to run a 2-week pilot starting early Jan. What's realistic?
[19:05] Ava: Early Jan kickoff is reasonable. We'll need sample app + traffic, and we'll propose a pilot scope doc. After pilot we'll run a performance deep-dive.
[19:15] Tom: Sounds good. Any compliance paperwork to start procurement?
[19:18] Ava: I'll share the security/compliance pack and a standard MSA. Procurement can start after we confirm pilot terms.
[19:25] (audio glitch) [19:30] Ravi: One last demo note - in TS you can enable typed responses with the schema option for structured output, helps a lot when building deterministic UIs.
[19:42] Priya: That's useful. We'll try structured outputs in the quickstart.
[19:47] Ava: Ok let's recap next steps.
[19:50] Ava: Action items - I'll send quickstart links (Python + TS), security docs, and pricing. Ravi will run a 1k-2k rps benchmark and suggest Dedicated sizing. Lena will share a sample app and traffic profile.
[20:05] Lena: We'll get the repo by Monday and confirm the pilot timeline.
[20:10] Priya: Thanks all, this was super helpful.
[20:13] Ava: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email. Bye.

Notes on transcript quality: automated captions had mis-typed some model names (rw-7b sometimes appears as raw-seven-b) and a few names were transcribed incorrectly; manual cleaning kept some imperfections to preserve realism.
